def: Continuing to train a pretrained model with next-token cross-entropy on demonstration prompts and responses, to teach a format and behaviour.
Training a policy to imitate an expert's actions directly, with no reward signal; SFT is behavioural cloning for language models.
The fixed recipe that turns a list of role-tagged messages into one token sequence using special tokens, which must match between training and serving.
Reserved vocabulary entries that mark structure, such as the start and end of a turn, rather than ordinary text.
Setting the labels of positions that should not be learned, such as the prompt, to an ignore value so they contribute no loss.
Concatenating several short training examples into one fixed-length row to avoid padding, which requires attention that does not cross example boundaries.
A batch loss averaged over every unmasked token, so long responses carry more total weight than short ones.
The loss of earlier abilities when a network is fine-tuned on new data, because all skills share the same weights.
Mixing a share of earlier training data into a new fine-tuning set to keep the old skills from degrading.
The claim, from the LIMA paper, that a model learns nearly all its knowledge in pretraining and that a small instruction set mainly teaches style and format.
Removing training examples that overlap evaluation sets so that benchmark scores do not simply measure memorisation.
